# localpsp

> A fake but stateful local server emulating Brazilian payment providers (Asaas first; Mercado Pago and Efí planned) for development and testing. Same endpoints, same payloads, same webhook signatures as the real API. Stateful: created charges persist and follow real lifecycles. Fires real webhooks at your local app, with the provider's real delivery semantics: retry schedule, duplicate deliveries with the same event id, and Asaas's queue interruption after 15 consecutive failures. Deterministic: same seed and virtual clock produce byte-identical event sequences, built for CI. Like localstripe or LocalStack, but for Brazilian PSPs.

Positioning: develop and run CI against localpsp; homologate against the provider's real sandbox once at the end. It kills the ngrok-plus-sandbox loop during development; it does not replace final homologation.

Sibling projects by the same author: EFCore.AutoSeed (.NET), autoseed (Go).

- Repo: github.com/danellalc/localpsp
- Distribution: Docker image (danellalc/localpsp) and single static binary
- Language-agnostic: your app talks HTTP to it; any stack works
- License: MIT
- Status: in development

## Quick start

```bash
docker run -p 8420:8420 danellalc/localpsp
```

Point your app's Asaas base URL at the emulator:

```
ASAAS_API_URL=http://localhost:8420/asaas/v3
```

Your existing integration code (SDK or raw HTTP) works unmodified, including webhook signature verification.

## CLI

```bash
localpsp trigger payment.confirmed --charge pay_123   # fire a lifecycle event webhook
localpsp trigger payment.received  --charge pay_123
localpsp clock advance 3d                              # virtual time; overdue events fire
localpsp state                                         # entities, deliveries, queue status
localpsp chaos duplicate-delivery --charge pay_123           # same event id, twice (idempotency test)
localpsp chaos retry-storm --charge pay_123 --failures 5     # exercise your backoff handling
localpsp chaos queue-interrupt --charge pay_123              # simulate Asaas pausing after 15 failures
localpsp chaos out-of-order --charge pay_123                 # CONFIRMED delivered after RECEIVED
```

## Key behaviors (the reason this exists)

- Webhook delivery counts as successful only on HTTP 2xx; otherwise the real retry schedule runs.
- After 15 consecutive failures the webhook queue pauses: new events accumulate but are not delivered, mirroring production Asaas. `localpsp state` shows it; reactivation mirrors the real flow.
- `PAYMENT_CONFIRMED` and `PAYMENT_RECEIVED` are distinct events, on purpose: in real Asaas, card settlement lands around D+32, so code that treats them as the same event risks double-crediting a customer. localpsp does not auto-fire `PAYMENT_RECEIVED` after any amount of virtual clock time; trigger it yourself with `localpsp trigger payment.received --charge <id>` whenever your test needs it.
- Deterministic: seed + virtual clock fully determine ids, timestamps, payloads and delivery order.

## Common mistakes when using this tool

- Do not skip final homologation on the real sandbox. localpsp accelerates development; the provider's checklist still applies.
- Do not use real API keys with localpsp; it accepts any key and never contacts real APIs.
- Do not test idempotency by triggering the event twice (that creates two events); use `chaos duplicate-delivery`, which re-sends the SAME event id.
- Do not rely on wall-clock time for lifecycle tests; use `localpsp clock advance`.
- Check FIDELITY.md for known divergences from the real API before assuming exact parity.

## Not supported

- Real API proxying or traffic recording.
- Real money movement of any kind.
- Providers beyond payments. Providers beyond Asaas are roadmap (Mercado Pago v2, Efí v3).
- Hosted/cloud version.
